newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close higher at another 6-yr peak.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close higher at another 6-yr peak.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed at another six-year high on Thursday, with strong market sentiment continuing to fuel buying and investors ignoring comments by the central bank governor on the market, brokers said.

The benchmark stock index ended 61.54 points, or 0.77 percent, higher to 8,081 points, surpassing the 8,059.14 finish on May 16, 1990 to the highest close since May 15, 1990's 8,569.55. Turnover was a hectic T$174.644 billion.
Electronics, electricals and machinery, and chemicals led other issues to become the day's bellwether shares, brokers said.
Electronics rose 1.87 percent with Acer gaining T$3 to T$66 and Ritek T$7 to T$112. Electricals and machinery rose 1.6 percent, with Hong Ho Precision edging up T$1.7 to T$26, they said.
Analysts said investors all but ignored central bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong's midmorning comment that he was "a bit worried" about the market's sizzling rally.
"Investors were optimistic to the performance of various sectors and not affected by the governor's comments," said Albert Lin of Golden Securities.

Despite his minor concern, Sheu told parliament he was willing to let investors determine stock values, calling the index rise above 8,000 "normal" in view of its 1990 crash to 2,500 points from over 12,600. Sheu vowed not to order measures to tighten loose liquidity in the money market.
"Sentiment remains bullish and will not be deterred easily. Investors are all eyeing the index's gains," said Allen Huang of National Securities.
"Unless there is concrete action from the central bank like tighening liquidity, verbal comments by the central bank appear less likely to dampen this strong sentiment," he added.
